subject: Surgical override request — forced-serving-mode & regional lock for CedarHealth integration
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Surgical override request — forced-serving-mode & regional lock for CedarHealth integration

Team,

CedarHealth (pilot customer, payer vertical) came back with an urgent regulator-driven requirement: their regulator requires that all inference for PHI-associated endpoints be served from a single verified model instance running in the EU region with NO AUTOMATIC FALLBACK to other model variants or regions. They need this enforced for production traffic starting next Monday (2028-06-25).

Ask: can we approve a "surgical override" (forced-serving-mode + regional lock, no-fallback) for the CedarHealth account for the following endpoints: /v1/claims-validate and /v1/clinical-summarize?

Why: regulator letter attached (Cedar_Health_regulatory_letter.pdf) — official directive; Cedar says they will sign an addendum (attached MAP: CH_MAP_v1.xlsx) and accept a limited SLA concession.

Constraints we already know:
- Expected QPS initially ~80 p50 latency target 350ms; burst to 250 QPS for scheduled job windows.
- Customer requests pinned model variant "ra-redwood-gpt-eu-1" (quantized)
- They explicitly disallow cross-region fallbacks and want a signed audit trail for every routing decision.

Immediate questions I need answered from product/eng/security:
1) Can the serving runtime enforce a hard region+variant lock for a single customer without automatic fallback?
2) What is the fastest safe path to get this live next week (canary plan / rollbacks / SLO adjustments)?
3) Security needs for audit logs, KMS usage, and proof for regulator — can we provide those artifacts in the timeline?

I'm looping legal (Laura) for contractual signoff and to confirm we can accept SLA carveouts. 

Next steps I propose:
- Product (Karthik): confirm feasibility + required config changes
- Eng (Marcus): estimate work and timeline for a locked rollout and canary plan
- Security (Irene): list required artifacts and whether we need a scoped exception in SOC2 controls

I know this is tight; please reply with the minimal set of blockers and any opt-in mitigation we should present to Cedar. I'll coordinate the customer comms once we have a plan.

Thanks,
Naomi
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Cedar_Health_regulatory_letter.pdf, CH_MAP_v1.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-18T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Surgical override request — forced-serving-mode & regional lock for CedarHealth integration

Naomi — thanks for the context and the attachments. I read the regulator letter. High level answers up front: yes we can implement a forced-serving configuration but there are trade-offs; details below.

Quick clarifying Qs for the customer that will affect the implementation:
- Do they require a hard blackhole (requests must fail if pinned variant unavailable) or a soft failure mode (requests queue or route to a holding path)? The wording matters for rollout.
- Will they accept a small maintenance window for kernel/quantized variant compilation if needed?

Technical implications (summary):
- Forced variant + region lock is supported by our routing layer as an override policy. However, removing fallback reduces reliability and will increase the probability of 503s if the pinned pool is overloaded or a node fails.
- For a 2x safety margin at 250 QPS bursts, we'll need to reserve dedicated capacity or guarantee pre-warmed GPUs (Dedicated or reserved pool).
- Telemetry: we can enable per-request routing audit logs (request_id, chosen_shard, model_variant, node_id, decision_reason) and retain them for 90 days. If regulator needs longer retention we'll need to expand storage.

Minimal plan to make next Monday feasible:
1) Engineering prepares a gated config change to add an account-specific override that pins model and region — ready by EOD Thursday if we prioritize.
2) Reserve a small dedicated pool for Cedar's endpoints (pre-warm 2 instances for failover). This requires ops approval and quota assignment.
3) Canary: route 5% traffic for 3 hours, monitor latency/error, then ramp to 100% in increments.

Risks:
- If the pinned variant requires a specific quantization kernel we might need a rebuild; that could add 48-72 hours.
- No-fallback increases risk of customer-visible outages. Need SLA concessions.

I can mobilize a small product/infra ship team to do the config change and the telemetry hooks; Marcus, can you confirm the capacity and kernel work estimate? Irene, confirm audit artifact details.

-Karthik
Director, Product — Serving
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-18T11:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Surgical override request — forced-serving-mode & regional lock for CedarHealth integration

Karthik / team — technical reply and runbook sketch below. TL;DR: feasible with conditions; full rollout safe in 7 business days if we accept limited kernel work in parallel.

What we need to ship:
- Routing config: account-scoped override (no-fallback flag + region pin) — changes confined to routing policy service, low-risk.
- Dedicated capacity: For 250 QPS bursts with 2x headroom, reserve 2x A100 equivalent slots in eu-west with pre-warm; this is an ops ticket (JIRA-OPS-4802).
- Model binary/quant kernel check: If the pinned variant already exists in our EU runtime image we can proceed immediately. If not, we need to build/validate the quant kernels (estimate 48 hours).
- Telemetry & audit: enable request-level routing logs and an append-only audit store for the account. We can store logs to the EU retention bucket (90 days by default).

Canary & rollback plan:
1) Create a canary config that pins traffic for a single shard (5% traffic) for 3 hours. Monitor: 95/99 latency, 5xx rate, KV-cache hit rate, memory pressure.
2) If canary healthy, step to 25% for 2 hrs, then 100% after sign-off.
3) If we see memory pressure or 5xx > 1%, trigger automatic rollback to previous routing policy (we must have a fallback path defined — note: customer asked NO fallback; we will still keep an internal emergency fallback for platform stability but that must be documented and disclosed to the customer as a break-glass option).

Work estimates (best effort):
- Routing policy change: 6 engineer-hours (timed at priority)
- Capacity reservation and pre-warm: depends on ops but request same-day approval
- Kernel build & validation (if required): 48–72 hours
- Telemetry / audit hooks: 8 engineer-hours + storage config

I will open the ops ticket and start the routing change today once I get formal approval. Attaching rollout_playbook.md (internal) for the detailed runbook.

-Marcus
Staff SWE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rollout_playbook.md

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-18T13:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Surgical override request — forced-serving-mode & regional lock for CedarHealth integration

Team — security/compliance constraints and required artifacts. Short answer: we can meet the regulator ask but need formal scoping and a small set of compensating controls.

Required artifacts we must provide to Cedar and to the regulator:
- Per-request routing audit log (immutable) showing timestamp, request_id, model_variant, node_id, routing_decision, and operator_id for any manual changes.
- Proof of EU data residency for both compute and audit store (we can place audit logs into eu-west retention bucket).
- KMS key usage record: keys must be EU-hosted or customer-managed (if they require customer KMS we need an integration window).
- SOC2 impact note: forced-region+no-fallback is an operational change that touches availability control; we need to record a scoped exception and update control narratives. This must be reviewed by our SOC2 lead and legal.

Compensating controls I recommend:
1) Short TTL for any emergency internal fallback (e.g., 15 minutes) with immediate pager alert and documented operator justification. Customer must sign off to allow any break-glass fallback.
2) Extended monitoring retention for 180 days for this account (regulator often requires longer audit trails). Budget impact — ops/storage will need to sign off.
3) Require the customer to sign an addendum accepting reduced availability SLA and to acknowledge break-glass condition.

I'll prepare a compliance package (artifact list + control exception doc) by EOD Friday if we commit to the change. Also need to sync with Legal (Laura) for contractual language.

-Irene
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Adam Chen <adam.chen@cedarhealth.com>, Samantha Rollins <samantha.rollins@cedarhealth.com>
Date: 2028-06-18T15:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Surgical override request — forced-serving-mode & regional lock for CedarHealth integration

All — after reading the thread and the regulator letter, legal is willing to approve a scoped, time-boxed surgical override for CedarHealth under the following conditions. This is a conditional sign-off; operations and security must confirm technical readiness and we must get a signed DocuSign addendum from Cedar before we change routing.

Conditions for approval:
1) Customer signs the addendum (CH_MAP_v1.xlsx) via DocuSign (link: https://docusign.com/RED-CH-approval-8921) acknowledging no automatic fallback and accepting the reduced availability SLA. Naomi, please confirm this is in flight.
2) Security provides the compliance package and we file a control exception ticket for SOC2 within 24 hours of rollout. Irene, please link the ticket back in this thread.
3) Engineering must implement the canary + automatic rollback triggers and ops must reserve the EU capacity before traffic is switched. Marcus — no rollout without the pre-warmed pool and the telemetry hooks.

If those three conditions are satisfied, legal authorizes the change for a 90-day trial period, after which we'll re-evaluate. Please keep me looped on the DocuSign signature and post the HubSpot deal update (HubSpot ID: CH-2345).

Naomi — I'd like you to coordinate the customer comms: outline the timeline (canary Tuesday morning EU time), the break-glass policy, and the acceptance of the SLA carveout. Once Adam or Samantha signs, we can trigger the ops ticket.

Thanks — Laura
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference
